body:
The description is a bit hard to follow and the steps are not clear, but this does seem expected, if a property is animated it is animated and controlled by the animation player as long as it is active

But if that's not the issue you are reporting please make the steps and description clearer and please add an MRP with specific details on what is expected and what does not work

It appears the cause is attempting to use both the AnimationTree and the AnimationPlayer which is referenced by the AnimationTree simultaneously.

This occurs because, as long as the AnimationTree is active, deterministic application is always prioritized every frame. Specifically, the AnimationTree's `ForceContinuous` option in CallbackModeDiscrete causes the SpriteFrame.animation track to perform ContinuousUpdate. Deterministic blending then sets the SpriteFrame.animation for all animations lacking a SpriteFrame.animation track to the RESET animation's SpriteFrame.animation value (if there is no RESET animation, type's default value so if it is String, become "") as the default value.

There are two ways: use only either the AnimationTree or the AnimationPlayer, or separate the Animations used by the AnimationTree and AnimationPlayer (means making 2 AnimationLibraries).

If you absolutely must use both simultaneously with only one AnimationLibrary, you need to understand the deterministic behavior and the Discrete setting, see also https://godotengine.org/article/migrating-animations-from-godot-4-0-to-4-3/#deterministic-blending.
